questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have family in the area, and I could access study programs at FU we don't have at KU- It was extremely helpful in order to get more knowledge in my field of study.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very nice subjects, very nice people. But I felt a little bit lost during my stay regarding the systems at FU. We got a brief introduction, but the teachers were not really aware of how to let me into the courses.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Some of it worked well - we had a tour and heard about the options at the university. But after that: It was difficult! The first days was okay, but I had the feeling that we were a little bit on our own at the department of Theater Studies. I had a hard time picking my subjects and I was not let into the Blackboard (teaching portal) for one of my subjects. I found the communication with the professors a little difficult - I still don't know how the formalities of the exam works, but they are very good people.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had a meeting with our coordinator.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Write in the groups of international people in Berlin!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I loved to be immersed in the city, but I was not a big part of the things going on at uni after school.

Additional comments:

questions.answer: I do not know what is meant by this. I described some of my experiences above.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I had a coordinator.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was successful, but it took a lot of effort and I still need final paperwork on the courses I participated in.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Show up and talk to the professors if you can't sign up online!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took MA classes, because I found that they suited my level and my interests. Also we start the university earlier in DK, so I was more sorrounded by people my age. I learned a lot! And also - they were in English.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different, more theory-oriented and a lot more focus on the texts.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
* Hope, Utopia and negativity
* Valeska Gert Guestprofessorship with Viktor Rubal
* Researching communities of practice: Fieldwork and histor. methods
* Choreographic Interventions

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Guest Professorship! REALLY a big experience.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to the nature parks on the border to Tjekkiet. Also - use the amazing free offers around the city. You can find good things on Rausgegangen (an app).
Go do something you never did before! I went to Qigong, saw my friend dance Flamenco, went to concerts. Say YES to opportunities <3 
Go to fleamarkets.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was harder than I thought, the city can be rough, but I eventually found my way. There are so many great things to do here.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
It takes time, but give it time and it will blossom <3 
Also - I met a girl in yoga class who is now a really good friend of mine - if you meet someone with a great energy, talk to them!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: That the people I encountered in the beginning seemed very closed off - but now I have really good friends.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: THE ARTSCENE!! And the possibility to eat out and have a coffee - the city is very vibrant.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Get to know the rules of the courses/exams/registration etc. ASAP
2. Be kind with yourself if it is hard to connect with people - it will come
3. READ THE MATERIAL!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just enjoy Grunewald every once in a while.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being in a very vibrant international environment. Performing at ADK with my class. Such a cool experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding out how the practical stuff works.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
